$comment: The claims copy lint (NFR-21, F-025, ADR-0031). Patterns live here rather than in scripts/verify-claims.mjs for the same reason recommendation weights are content: this list will grow, and growing it should not be a code change. Read by scripts/verify-claims.mjs and exercised by scripts/verify-claims-proof.mjs.

banned.why: A camera estimate is not exact. The word promises a precision the hardware cannot deliver, and it is the single most common overstatement in this product category.

Implies one authoritative answer exists and we found it. A rendered hex is a modern approximation of a colour a dye produced on a fibre under daylight. Use 'specified' for a colorimetric value, 'estimated' for a capture.

Same claim as 'true colour' wearing a plainer word; ADR-0031 bans it for the estimated source. The determiner is REQUIRED in the pattern: 'covers actual colours' means real-world colours as against synthetic test values, which is ordinary English and not a claim. Without it the gate fires on its own ADR.
A percentage with no device, no illuminant, no sample size and no dE00 distribution behind it. No number without a row (NFR-2).
Naming returns a closest reference ranked by dE00. There is no match, perfect or otherwise (FR-7).
Borrows the authority of a laboratory instrument for a phone camera.
Permitted only inside calibrated mode with a measurement behind it. Everywhere else it is a claim about hardware we do not control.
Nothing about consumer camera capture is guaranteed. Note this pattern is deliberately narrow: 'guaranteed' about a deterministic property of the ENGINE is true and permitted.
The core is colour science and explicit rules (ADR-0002). The phrase is both inaccurate here and the category's standard evasion.
'Measured' is reserved for the calibrated and reference sources. An estimate is estimated.
An identifier is as much a violation as a button label. A name propagates into a field, then into a stored record, then into copy — and by then nobody remembers it was a shorthand.
Mirrors `exact-colour`. A camera estimate is not exact, and this is the same promise about a precision the hardware cannot deliver.
Mirrors `true-colour`. It implies one authoritative answer exists and we found it; a rendered hex is a modern approximation of a colour a dye once produced.
Mirrors `perfect-match`. Naming returns a closest reference ranked by dE00 — there is no such thing to promise (FR-7).
Mirrors `percent-accurate`. A figure like this needs a device-lab row behind it (NFR-2) and there are none.
Mirrors `guaranteed-accuracy`. Nothing about a camera reading can be guaranteed, and the word is the category standard for saying so anyway.

banned.pattern: (プロ仕様|業務用品質|プロ品質)
banned.why: Mirrors `professional-grade`. It claims a standard nobody set and nobody measured.
Mirrors `ai-powered`. The core is colour science and explicit rules (ADR-0002); the English pattern cannot match this because the phrase is written in Latin letters inside Japanese text.

FR-72's own words: an equivalent is never described as a match. The nearest member of a curated palette by dE00 is a distance, not an identity — the same distinction FR-7 draws for naming, and the reason this feature keeps computed and editorial apart in the first place.

banned.pattern: (この|その)色(と|に)(完全|ぴったり)?(一致|マッチ)
banned.why: Mirrors `equivalent-is-a-match`. A contemporary equivalent is the nearest reference by dE00 or a recorded editorial judgement; neither asserts that one colour IS another.

A percentage offered as a match reads as a probability of identity. Naming returns the closest reference ranked by ΔE00 and never a match (FR-7), and a figure bolted onto the honest distance is what makes the invented half credible. Mockup 03 draws '97% Match' beside ΔE00 1.18; 07 and 13 put 'Match' after the personal-fit figure. CAUGHT — each of these is a line of packages/testing/fixtures/claims/variants.md that the proof requires refused: a figure before 'match' ('97% close match', '97%-match', '97 per cent match'); 'match' before a figure ('Match: 97%', 'Match (97%)', 'Match — 97%', 'Match: 97/100', 'Match 0.97'); a chance, likelihood or probability of a match; a percentage 'identical' or 'the same colour'; a figure written as a placeholder or expression in the SAME source line. LEFT ALONE — each is a line of near-misses.md: a proportion of things that match ('84% of outfits match your profile', '(32%) match your palette'); the SIMILARITY percentage FR-7 requires and ADR-0048 defines ('94% similar', '3 matches · 97% similar'). A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

The same claim in Japanese. CAUGHT (variants.md): 97%一致, 97%の一致, 97パーセント一致, ９７％一致, 一致率97%, 一致率は約97%, 一致度はおよそ97%, マッチ度97%, マッチング率97%, 合致率97%, 97%の確率で一致, 97％でマッチ, 類似度97%で一致, 92%（クールミュートに一致）. LEFT ALONE (near-misses.md): 類似度97% — the similarity percentage FR-7 requires — and 一致する服が3着あります. A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

Separation (FR-5) is a score for specific colours under a simulation model. Calling a palette safe, friendly, proof, accessible or approved for a colour-vision deficiency, or distinguishable by everyone, is a claim about every person with that deficiency, which no model supports. Mockups 00, 07, 08, 10, 13, 15 and 16 draw it. CAUGHT (variants.md): a colour-vision term followed by safe, friendly, proof, accessible or approved ('Protan/Deutan Safe', 'CVD-proof', 'colour-blind accessible'); 'safe' after a deficiency name behind a colon, dash, bullet or bracket ('Protanopia — Safe', 'Deuteranopia (Safe)'); 'safe' within six characters after 'separation'; safe for, across or under a deficiency or all its types; a percentage offered as distinction; fully, entirely, always or guaranteed distinguishable; everyone, anyone or every such user able to tell colours apart. LEFT ALONE (near-misses.md): capability copy ('100% CVD simulation', 'Colour-blind mode'), and a claim word directly after 'not', 'n't' or 'never' — the honest warning the product must be free to give ('may not be fully distinguishable', 'Not CVD-safe: separation 18'). A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

The same absolute claim about colour vision, in Japanese. CAUGHT (variants.md): 色覚特性に100%対応, すべての色覚で区別可能, すべての色覚タイプで見分けられます, P型・D型に安全, CVD安全, CVDセーフ, 色覚に安全, 色覚障害の方でも安心, 分離92%（安全）, 92%分離（セーフ）, CVD識別：100%, 誰でも・どなたでも見分けられる, 色覚を問わず・に関わらず識別可能, 色覚特性があっても区別できます, カラーユニバーサルデザイン対応, 色覚バリアフリー. LEFT ALONE (near-misses.md): 完全に安全 about data on the device, 区別しやすさ as a noun, CVD安全性 as a topic, 色覚に配慮した配色, and a claim followed within fourteen characters by a negation (とは限りません, できない, わけではありません). A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

A composite score presented as a verdict. FR-32 shows every component and never lets the overall replace them. Mockups 08 and 13 draw it. CAUGHT (variants.md): a verdict adjective before 'harmony', with a space or a hyphen ('Master Harmony', 'Master-Harmony', 'Beautiful harmony'); 'Harmony' followed by a verdict behind a colon, dash, bullet, bar or bracket; 'Harmonious Pairing'; a score or figure followed by a separator and a verdict, a word + 'Harmony', or a letter grade ('Outfit Score: 93 / 100 • Excellent', '• Strong Harmony', '• A+', 'Lc 48 • Optimal'); 'Perfect Outfit'. LEFT ALONE (near-misses.md): the relationship names (FR-6) in any punctuation ('Harmony: analogous', 'Harmony · analogous'), 'Harmony score 82', 'Master the harmony of kasane layering', 'Perfect for autumn'. A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

banned.pattern: (?:完璧な|最高の|究極の|完全な|理想的な|パーフェクトな?|見事な|抜群の|至高の|極上の|絶妙な|素晴らしい)\s*(?:調和|ハーモニー)|(?:マスター|アルティメット|エクセレント|パーフェクト)[・\s]?ハーモニー|(?:調和|ハーモニー)(?:度|スコア)?\s*[:：]\s*(?:完璧|最高|パーフェクト|エクセレント|抜群|見事|究極|優秀|最適)|完璧に調和|調和の(?:とれた|取れた)(?:組み合わせ|組合せ|ペア|配色|コーデ)|スコア[^。\n]{0,12}?[0-9０-９]+\s*(?:[\/／]\s*100)?\s*[・•·—]\s*(?:完璧|最高|抜群|マスター|パーフェクト|優秀|最適|素晴らしい)|[0-9０-９]\s*[・•·—|]\s*(?:最適|優秀|完璧|最高|抜群)
banned.why: The same verdict in Japanese, including the Japanese forms of both drawn verdicts — 1.48:1・非テキスト／調和のとれた組み合わせ (08) and 90%（APCA Lc 48・最適） (13). CAUGHT (variants.md): マスターハーモニー, 完璧な調和, 素晴らしい調和, 見事な調和, 調和：完璧, 調和：優秀, 調和スコア：最高, 完璧に調和, 調和のとれた組み合わせ, a score followed by a verdict (総合スコア 93 / 100・優秀), and a figure followed by a separator and 最適 or 優秀. LEFT ALONE (near-misses.md): the relationship names (類似色の調和, 補色の調和, 調和：類似色). A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

Grade, standard or approval borrowed from an institution or an instrument — for a phone and a PDF, as `professional-grade` borrows a profession's. Mockup 18 draws 'Museum-grade' twice. CAUGHT (variants.md): an institution or instrument word — museum, gallery, archive, conservation, conservator, hospital, clinical, medical, lab, scientific, industrial, instrument, colorimeter, pro — joined to grade, quality, level, standard, worthy, class, caliber, approved or certified ('museum-caliber', 'Museum-approved', 'conservator-grade'); any grade, level or class applied to accuracy or precision ('Pantone-level accuracy', 'Industrial-grade colour accuracy'); lab or instrument precision; parity with an instrument ('as accurate as a colorimeter', 'Rivals a spectrophotometer'); 'trusted by' or 'used by' museums or labs. LEFT ALONE (near-misses.md): research- and reference-grade (ADR-0061's honest use; 'reference' is a provenance source); a studio, which is a lighting condition; enterprise-grade, the owner's own quality bar; 'the PDF/A archival standard' and 'the CIE Lab standard observer', which name real standards; and a disclaimer with 'not', 'n't', 'never' or 'no' up to 24 characters before ('This isn't a medical-grade colour-vision test', 'no substitute for a clinical-level eye exam'). A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

banned.pattern: (?:美術館|博物館|研究所|研究室|研究機関|医療機関|医療用?|臨床|ミュージアム|ギャラリー|ラボ|測色計|測色器|色彩計|色彩色差計|計測器|分光光度計|分光測色計|業務用)(?:品質|グレード|級|クオリティ|レベル|並み|仕様|クラス)(?![^。\n]{0,10}(?:ではありません|ではない|ではなく|じゃない))|(?:分光測色計|分光光度計|測色計|測色器|色彩計|色彩色差計|計測器|測定器)(?:に匹敵|と同等|並み|に迫る)[^。\n]{0,4}(?:精度|正確)
banned.why: The same borrowed authority in Japanese. CAUGHT (variants.md): an institution or instrument — 美術館, 博物館, 研究所, 研究機関, 医療機関, 医療用, ラボ, 測色計, 測色器, 色彩計, 色彩色差計, 計測器, 分光光度計, 業務用 — joined to 品質, グレード, 級, レベル, 並み, 仕様 or クラス; parity with an instrument (分光測色計に匹敵する精度, 計測器と同等の精度, 測色計に迫る精度). LEFT ALONE (near-misses.md): 測定器レベルの値を入力 — the measure screen asks a person to enter values from their own instrument; 高品質; and a disclaimer followed within ten characters by ではありません or ではない (医療グレードの検査ではありません). A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

An RGB camera measures no spectrum. Saying the product captures, measures, extracts, analyses, reads, scans, detects, samples, recovers, reconstructs, estimates or infers one — or reflectance — names a physical quantity the pipeline never measures; mockup 27's loading state says 'Extracting reflectance spectra'. CAUGHT (variants.md): one of those verbs before a spectrum or reflectance, with up to one word between ('Analysing the fabric spectrum', 'Reconstructing spectra from RGB'); a spectral profile, scan, reading, reconstruction, estimation, imaging or power distribution; a spectrum scan or analysis; hyperspectral or multispectral. LEFT ALONE (near-misses.md): the bare noun 'spectral data'; 'Estimated reflectance is not available from a phone camera'; 'the full spectrum of seasonal colours'. A sentence that denies the measurement with the verb names it, and takes `claims-ok:` as every refusal does. A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

banned.pattern: 分光(?:反射率|測定(?!器)|分析|計測|スキャン)|分光(?:特性|分布|情報|データ)[をの]?(?:解析|分析|測定|計測|取得|抽出|推定)|反射スペクトル|反射率[をの]?(?:測定|計測|取得)|スペクトル(?:データ|情報)?[をの]?(?:解析|分析|測定|計測|スキャン|抽出|取得|読み取|推定)
banned.why: The same unmeasured quantity in Japanese. CAUGHT (variants.md): 分光反射率, 分光測定, 分光分析, 分光計測, 分光特性を解析, 分光分布を測定, 反射スペクトル, 反射率の測定, スペクトル解析, スペクトルの解析中, スペクトル推定, スペクトル情報を取得, スペクトルを抽出, 分光データを取得. LEFT ALONE (near-misses.md): スペクトル and 分光データ as nouns — the honest statement that there are none — and 分光測定器, the instrument whose readings the measure screen asks a person to enter. A form in neither file is not known either way (F-219).

provenanceLanguage.$comment: ADR-0031 section 1. NOT YET ENFORCED, and F-017 moved this from F-017 to F-040 rather than enforcing it. The render tree now exists, so the mechanism is no longer the blocker — the DATA is. This table is conditional on Provenance.source, and every colour any surface can render today is `declared`: the home screen's samples are declared constants and the corpus is empty. A check whose interesting branches — calibrated, estimated, unknown — cannot be reached would be green because nothing exercises it, which is indistinguishable from being green because the copy is correct. The Lens (F-040) is what first produces an estimated value with a confidence beside it, and that is when the check can discriminate. Recorded here as data so the table exists before the check does, and the lint prints on every run that this half is unenforced.

derived.$comment: ADR-0100. A colour this engine computed from another colour. It was never observed, so the bans are stronger than `declared`’s: "detected" and "sampled" both assert an observation, and "measured" is reserved for calibrated and reference under ADR-0031 section 1 regardless. What it MAY say is what it is — that a machine worked it out.

allowlist.$comment: Three KINDS, deliberately not interchangeable. A blanket path exemption for 'docs that discuss the policy' would swallow every real claim in docs/, so policySource is an explicit file list and nothing else.

policySource.why: The decision record that bans these constructions. It must state them.
The governance document implementing ADR-0031.
This file. The patterns are its content.
The lint. It reports what it found, which means printing it.
The mutation proof. It plants each construction deliberately.
The skill teaching the policy.
Teaches copy discipline in both locales; quotes the banned list.
Quotes the accuracy-claim rule for engine work.
Binding rules for packages/color-*; restates the claims discipline.
Restates the rule for comments and identifiers.
Subagent brief carrying the same prohibition.
Scoped harness for the strictest zone; restates the rule.
This feature's plan. Names the constructions it bans.
Append-only history. Records where the rule was applied and why, including the phrases corrected.
Records the naming-is-never-identity decision and the language it rejected.
NFR-21 states the banned constructions as its own acceptance condition.
The voice guide. Its whole table is a never-say list with replacements.
Constraint C11 enumerates the claims the product may not make.
Teaches never to convert a dE distribution into a percentage; must quote the norm it rejects.
Records the category norm we differentiate against by refusing it.
This feature's plan. Names the constructions it bans, as F-025's does.

allowlist.$measuredComment: EMPTY, and that is the correct state. A `measured` entry exempts an actual accuracy claim, and requires `claim`, `measurement` (a link to the device-lab row) and `why`. There are no measurements yet — the device colour lab is F-063 — so there can be no permitted claim. The lint prints this count on every run so an empty allowlist cannot be mistaken for a thorough one.

inlineMarker.$comment: For a line that FORBIDS a construction or records its deliberate absence — `no isExactMatch`, `never say "exact colour"`. Requires a reason after the token on the same line; a bare marker is itself a failure, because an exemption nobody had to justify is not an exemption. NOTE for prose ABOUT this mechanism: the token includes the colon deliberately, so write `claims-ok` without it when discussing the marker rather than using it. Otherwise every document explaining the marker trips the bare-marker check and the policySource list grows one entry per author. Found the first time a plan described it.
